The memory was too fresh, too pointed.

But never mind that, for I have such news! You will never guess, Lady Everleigh, whom I encountered just this very morning, not ten minutes past, walking quite alone, near the old elm by the common. Lady Everleigh, ever polite, obliged with a gentle, “Indeed, Mrs. Gable? Do tell us.”

One does so hope not, for the sake of the family, and young Mr. Dalton’s prospects, of course!” She finally drew a breath, perhaps for the first time since entering the room, and then, catching sight of the painting, exclaimed, “Good heavens, Lady Everleigh, what a charming new acquisition! Is it not a little dark for the drawing-room, though? One likes something with a little more cheer, does one not? Though I daresay the frame is quite handsome.”

Perhaps its very solemnity lends it a certain contemplative grace, a quality not always to be found in brighter scenes.” He glanced at Beatrice, a fleeting, almost imperceptible gleam in his eye, as if inviting her complicity in this subtle parrying. Beatrice, however, remained outwardly impassive, though inwardly she acknowledged the shrewdness of his retort. He is not, I think, a man to content himself with conventional arrangements. He enjoys a certain degree of intrigue, a hint of the clandestine. And his attentions to Miss Fairfax, though subtle, were, to my eye, rather too consistent to be merely casual. There is a thread of admiration there, a quiet, almost possessive regard, that speaks of something more than mere acquaintance.”
